paper.title: Calculation of Optimum Parameters for Alternating Direction Implicit Procedures (Algorithm 460)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 16(10), p. 633 (Oct 1973), per the frame item and the shipped 460.gz shar header (which cites Communications of the ACM 16(10) pp. 633-635)
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/460.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used). Frame item prints the second author as '. D. Sebastian'; the first name is not verified.

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 460.gz (shell archive dated 2005-12-15 by its header; Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f, Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f, Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res, Fortran/Dp/Drivers/Makefile)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/460.gz (HTTP 200, gzip, original size 8937 bytes). sha256 of 460.gz: 542ae8263c1d41ae98a2d100713e8dc62555d50ee88446d28c2b608002c8982d (scout download, 2026-11-27).
code.note: Gunzip the archive, then unpack the shell archive with /bin/sh in an empty directory (the shar begins at the #! /bin/sh line). Build Fortran/Dp/Src/src.f with Fortran/Dp/Drivers/driver.f (the Makefile does this), run the driver from Fortran/Dp/Drivers, and compare its output with the shipped Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res file.

field: numerics (alternating direction implicit iteration, optimal ADI acceleration parameters)

claim.location: Shipped reference output Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res (inside 460.gz), the first table 'Given ITNS, compute DMU', row ITNS = 1: DMU = 0.775958E-01 (ier = 0). The driver calls adip (iopt = 1) for ITNS = 1..5 with a = 0.5, b = 2.0, c = 0.25, d = 0.75, n = 10, and prints the computed DMU in g14.6 format.

reference.file: Fortran/Dp/Drivers/res (inside 460.gz), the line for ITNS = 1 in the first table
reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: Value 0.0775958 (printed 0.775958E-01) at the ITNS = 1 row of the shipped res file, as printed by the shipped driver (6 significant digits). The paper's table is not read; the claim is the code's own printed output.
claim.metric: The DMU printed by driver.f for ITNS = 1 in the 'Given ITNS, compute DMU' block, compared as an absolute number with 0.0775958
claim.determinism: deterministic (adip is a closed computation on fixed a, b, c, d and n; no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The shipped value is printed with 6 significant digits, so the print rounding alone is at most 5e-8 in absolute terms at this magnitude; 1e-7 covers that and nothing more. A changed ADI parameter formula or iteration count moves DMU by far more than 1e-7 (the next row is 0.150983E-02 for ITNS = 2). Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one Fortran compile and one driver run of a few dozen calls to adip with n = 10.
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices (the rerun should record it).

why: The shipped driver computes the optimal ADI parameter DMU for a given iteration count by running the adip routine, and its printed value is the code's own output, so the rerun has to execute the Fortran method to reproduce it.
